ai.title: Show premium-session quota in CLI session-ended banner
ai.summary: CLI session-ended banner now displays "N of M premium sessions used today" alongside the status. `getRateLimitsByModel` helper added to `common/src/types/freebuff-session.ts` to extract quota snapshots from queued, active, and ended states. `markFreebuffSessionEnded` preserves prior `rateLimitsByModel` data to populate the banner without extra fetches. Server-side `attachRateLimit` extended to include quota data in `ended` responses.

eli5.text: After a free premium session ends, the goodbye screen now tells you how many of your daily premium sessions you've used, like "2 of 3 premium sessions used today," instead of just saying the session ended. This number updates live while you wait in line and when your session finishes, and if you've used all your daily allowances, the screen border turns amber to signal you've hit the cap. The count can show fractions (for example, 1.3 if a session ran long) but always matches the daily limit shown alongside it. This is live today for anyone using the free tier of premium models, and you'll notice it both in the waiting room while your turn is coming up and on the final banner once your session is done.

ai.title: base2 free orchestrators derive reviewer agent id from model
ai.summary: base2.ts now resolves freeCodeReviewerAgentId via FREEBUFF_REVIEWER_AGENT_ID_BY_MODEL[model] lookup instead of accepting explicit freeCodeReviewerAgentId parameter. The freeCodeReviewerAgentId option removed from createBase2 signature. base2-free-deepseek.ts, base2-free-kimi.ts, base2-free.ts drop hardcoded reviewer agent id values (code-reviewer-deepseek, code-reviewer-kimi, code-reviewer-minimax) that previously shadowed the default code-reviewer-lite. Fallback to code-reviewer-lite preserved for unmapped models.

eli5.text: You no longer manually pick which assistant reviews your code when using the free version, the system now automatically chooses the right reviewer AI based on which main AI you selected. Behind the scenes, instead of typing a specific reviewer name into your setup (like telling a librarian exactly which shelf to check), the orchestrator now looks up the matching expert for whatever AI model you picked, falling back to the default "lite" reviewer if your model doesn't have a specialized one assigned yet.

ai.title: Restore CLI diff viewer rendering
ai.summary: Removed `RENDER_DIFFS` flag and associated null-return check in `cli/src/components/tools/diff-viewer.tsx`. Diff viewer now unconditionally renders `diffText` lines with theme colors. Scope limited to CLI component logic.

eli5.text: The command-line tool used to show you a blank space where file changes should appear, and now it actually shows those changes again with colored lines marking what was added or removed. A hidden setting had been turned off, telling the tool to skip drawing the diff entirely, and that setting and its skip-check have been removed so the diff display runs normally again. If you use the CLI to review changes, you will see the expected added/removed text with the usual theme colors instead of an empty area.

ai.title: CLI /history: Fix up delete buttons
ai.summary: The CLI `/history` delete button now renders as `[×]` instead of `Delete`, with layout width adjusted to 6 chars. `padRight` switched to `Array.from` for code-point counting, preventing emoji/wide-character padding breakage. Reserved width calculation now accounts for border, scrollbar, and button padding explicitly. SelectableList row styling removed `width: 100%` in favor of flex properties and added `marginRight` to the action button.

eli5.text: When you open the chat history list in the CLI, the button that used to say Delete now shows as a small x icon, and the row layout has been adjusted so the prompt text column expands more reliably. The spacing math now accounts for the list border, scrollbar, and button padding, so rows with emojis or wide characters no longer shift the text around. Youll notice the rows look more evenly padded and the delete button takes up less horizontal space, leaving more room for your chat titles to be visible.

ai.title: Freebuff 0.0.84 release version bump
ai.summary: The Freebuff CLI release manifest version was bumped from 0.0.83 to 0.0.84. This version bump packages five user-visible CLI improvements that shipped in the surrounding commits: chat history deletion support, premium-session quota display in the session-ended banner, reviewer agent id derivation by model in base2 free orchestrators, restored diff viewer rendering, and fixed /history delete button layout.
ai.evidence: Modified file `freebuff/cli/release/package.json` shows version field changed from `0.0.83` to `0.0.84`, a single-line release bump in the CLI release manifest.

eli5.text: Freebuff 0.0.84 adds the ability to delete individual chat conversations directly from your chat history screen, and it now shows you how many of your premium AI sessions have been used each day right in the session-ended banner so you can track your quota. The built-in code reviewer agents are now automatically matched to the AI model you pick, so free reviews use the right lightweight reviewer without extra setup, and the side-by-side code diff viewer renders again after a glitch was fixed. Upgrading gives you cleaner chat history management, clearer visibility into your daily premium session limits, and more reliable diff viewing whenever the CLI shows you what changed in your files.

ai.title: Freebuff 1.0.673 release bundles history deletion, premium quota
ai.summary: The 1.0.673 release (cli/release/package.json version bump from 1.0.672) packages five user-visible changes into the codebuff binary. The CLI chat history screen now supports a delete action through deleteChatSession with path-traversal validation and immediate UI updates. The session-ended banner reports premium session quota as "N of M premium sessions used today" via a new getRateLimitsByModel helper that snapshots rateLimitsByModel from queued, active, and ended states. Base2 free orchestrators now resolve the reviewer agent id through a FREEBUFF_REVIEWER_AGENT_ID_BY_MODEL lookup, dropping hardcoded ids and falling back to code-reviewer-lite for unmapped models. Additionally, the diff viewer unconditionally renders diffText lines after removing the RENDER_DIFFS flag, and the /history delete button renders as [×] with 6-character width using Array.from-based code-point padding.
ai.evidence: Commit 26432edc modifies only cli/release/package.json, incrementing the codebuff version field from 1.0.672 to 1.0.673 (a one-line release-bump with +1/-1 stats).

eli5.text: This release lets you take back control of your chat history and see exactly how much premium usage you've gotten, all while making the coding assistant pick the right review partner automatically. You can now permanently delete individual conversations from your chat history screen, so old sessions no longer clutter your list or take up space. When a chatting session ends, a banner now shows how many of your daily premium sessions you've used, giving you a real-time snapshot of your allowance without leaving the terminal. The assistant behind the scenes now automatically selects the best code reviewer for the AI model you're using, dropping old hardcoded defaults that sometimes shadowed the intended lightweight reviewer. The side-by-side diff viewer, which had gone dark, now reliably renders code changes again with proper theme colors. Finally, the delete button in the history list got a visual refresh, now showing as a clean "[×]" and laying out correctly even with emoji and wide characters.

ai.title: Add disabled OpenCode Zen provider scaffold
ai.summary: OpenCode Zen provider scaffold added but disabled. Models opencode/minimax-m2.7 and opencode/kimi-k2.6 defined in common/src/constants/model-config.ts. Chat completions API returns 400 error 'opencode_zen_disabled' for these models in web/src/app/api/v1/chat/completions/_post.ts. OPENCODE_API_KEY added to env schema and .env.example.

eli5.text: If you ask the assistant to use the new model options 'minimax-m2.7' or 'kimi-k2.6', it will refuse and return an error saying those models are currently disabled, even if you have an API key for them in your settings file. The system has been taught about these models so it recognizes them, but the actual connection to talk to that provider is blocked behind a switch, so nothing actually works yet for users on any plan.

ai.title: Enable codex goals and collaboration modes
ai.summary: Added .codex/config.toml enabling goals and collaboration_modes features. Applies to codex subsystem configuration. Sets feature flags to true.

eli5.text: You can now ask the assistant to work toward a specific goal and set it to a more collaborative mode where it checks in with you. This is an internal configuration change that turns on two new capabilities in the system. Nothing breaks, and you'd see this if you used those modes.

ai.title: Enable OpenCode Zen for opencode/ prefixed models
ai.summary: OpenCode Zen routing now activates for any model string starting with `opencode/` instead of a hardcoded allowlist. The `isOpenCodeZenModel` check uses `startsWith`, and `getOpenCodeZenModelId` strips the prefix for unknown models. The disabled-model validation gate in `_post.ts` is removed, allowing these requests to proceed to stream/non-stream handlers.

eli5.text: If you ask for a model whose name starts with the prefix "opencode/", the system will now process that request instead of turning it away with an error. You would notice that previously blocked model requests now return a real response rather than a "currently disabled" message. This affects any model request using that specific prefix going forward.

ai.title: Type guard in isOpenCodeZenModel
ai.summary: isOpenCodeZenModel signature changed to `model: unknown` with return type `model is string`. Added `typeof model === 'string'` check before prefix validation. Fixes type errors in completions.test.ts and opencode-zen.ts. Internal refactor, no user-visible behavior change.

eli5.text: The helper that checks whether a chosen AI model belongs to the internal OpenCode Zen family now rejects anything that isn't a plain text model name before looking for the special prefix, instead of trusting that it was always given a text name. This only touches the behind-the-scenes code that runs model lookups, so nothing you see or do changes; it just prevents the program from breaking when an unexpected value is handed to that check. It's live today as part of the current release.

ai.title: Fix completions test dev localhost bypass
ai.summary: Updated `completions.test.ts` to inject `cf-connecting-ip: 192.0.2.1` in the unknown-location test. This bypasses the dev-only localhost check that triggers when `cf-ipcountry` and client IP are absent. Assertion updated to expect `unresolved_client_ip` instead of `missing_client_ip`. Scope limited to `web/src/app/api/v1/chat/completions/__tests__/completions.test.ts`.

eli5.text: The system was updated to properly handle a test case where it checks what happens when a free user's location can't be determined. Previously, the test relied on a special dev mode bypass that would activate when no location data was found and the request came from a local machine. Now it uses a specific fake internet address that can't be mapped to any real location, so the test accurately reflects what happens for real users whose locations can't be identified. If you looked at this test, you'd see it now sends an extra header to simulate a real unknown visitor, and it checks for the correct rejection message that matches real-world behavior instead of the old dev-only shortcut.

ai.title: Legacy CLI auth code parsing
ai.summary: Added regex fallback in `parseAuthCode` to handle legacy hyphen-delimited auth codes when dot separators are missing. This prevents auth failures for older CLI clients by extracting `fingerprintId`, `expiresAt`, and `receivedHash` from the legacy format. Changes apply to `web/src/app/onboard/_helpers.ts` and `freebuff/web/src/app/onboard/_helpers.ts`. Logging in `onboard/page.tsx` now includes `dotCount` and `hyphenCount` to aid debugging of malformed codes.

eli5.text: When signing in with an older command-line version of the tool, the login code it sends no longer causes a sign-in failure. The system now recognizes the legacy two-part code format (using hyphens instead of dots) and correctly reads the three pieces of information from it. If you use the latest version, nothing changes; if you use an older command-line client, you can now log in successfully again.

ai.title: CLI auth codes use opaque tokens
ai.summary: CLI login flow now issues random 32-byte base64url tokens instead of exposing raw fingerprint auth codes. Tokens stored in verificationToken table with cli-login: prefix and expiry. Onboard page resolves token to auth code via getCliAuthCodeForToken, falling back to raw code for backward compatibility. Covers freebuff/web and web packages.

eli5.text: When you sign in to the service from the command-line tool, the system now gives you a random, scrambled code instead of a structured one that reveals internal tracking details. The scrambled code gets stored in the system's record-keeping, and when the web page confirms your login, it looks up the scrambled code to find the real internal code it needs, while still accepting the old-style codes for anything that hasn't updated yet. You'll notice no difference in how you sign in, but the codes you receive are now unreadable to anyone who might intercept them.
